sections.h2: Meriden and the Silver City name
sections.html:
Meriden is a New Haven County city roughly halfway between New Haven and Hartford. It had 60,850 residents in 2020 and covers about 24 square miles. In the second half of the 1800s the city turned out silver, lamps, glassware, guns, cutlery and musical instruments. The Meriden Britannia Company and its successor, the International Silver Company, earned it the Silver City label, and International Silver kept producing into the early 1980s.

Meriden was part of Wallingford until it gained its own meetinghouse in 1727, became a town in 1806 and a city in 1867. The oldest house in town is the Solomon Goffe House, built in 1711, which became a museum in 1986.

Meriden sits on the Metacomet Ridge, a trap rock ridgeline that runs from Long Island Sound toward Vermont. The Hanging Hills, with West Peak, East Peak and South Mountain, rise inside the city, and Castle Craig stands in Hubbard Park, dedicated in 1900. The Quinnipiac River runs through South Meriden, passing through a gorge, and Harbor Brook crosses the city and empties into Hanover Pond. Meriden Center and South Meriden are the principal communities.

Lots therefore vary. Some are on hillsides near trails, and others sit lower, near the Quinnipiac or Harbor Brook, where a buyer may ask about drainage.

  • Hubbard Park and the Hanging Hills on the north and west side.
  • Giuffrida Park, with hiking trails and a lake.
  • Quinnipiac River Gorge Trail and Hanover Pond Trail in South Meriden.

In 2020, 7.0 percent of units were vacant, with a rental vacancy rate of 6.5 percent and a homeowner vacancy rate of 1.5 percent. About 30.4 percent of households were one person living alone, while much of the stock is older and family-sized. Survey values like these say little about what any one house will bring.

Meriden is on Interstate 91, which links it to Hartford, Springfield and New Haven. Interstate 691 heads west toward Interstate 84 and Waterbury, and the Wilbur Cross Parkway (Route 15) runs southwest toward New Haven. U.S. Route 5 passes through as North and South Broad Street.

The Meriden Transit Center is downtown on the New Haven to Springfield line, served by the CT Rail Hartford Line and by Amtrak, including the Northeast Regional, Valley Flyer and Vermonter.

  • CT Transit buses A, B and C loop through the city once per hour, with connections to New Britain, Hartford and New Haven.
  • Meriden Markham Municipal Airport, about three miles south of the center, serves private and charter planes.
  • Bradley International Airport and Tweed New Haven Airport are the nearest commercial airports.

Rail access and highway position help with commuters, but the house itself sets the price, and a rail-adjacent address does not fix condition problems.

The Meriden Board of Education runs eight elementary schools (K to 5): John Barry, Benjamin Franklin, Nathan Hale, Hanover, Thomas Hooker, Casimir Pulaski, Israel Putnam and Roger Sherman. Lincoln, Washington and Edison are the middle schools, and the public high schools are Francis T. Maloney and Orville H. Platt. H. C. Wilcox is a Connecticut technical high school. Confirm current assignments with the district before you quote them to a buyer.

sections.h2: Tax installments, liens and the revaluation
sections.html:
Meriden bills real estate in four equal installments, due in July, October, January and April. Bills are mailed only once a year, in July, so keep it for the later installments. Taxable property is listed as of each October 1, and taxes on that list are due the following July 1.

Interest on late taxes runs at 1.5 percent a month, which the city describes as 18 percent a year. Real estate taxes still unpaid at the end of the year in which they are due must be liened against the property, and the city will not issue building permits on a property with that kind of debt. Water and sewer bills, due in March, June, September and December, can also lead to liens and a recommendation to foreclose.

The latest citywide revaluation applies to the October 1, 2025 Grand List, and appraisers studied sales from the 24 months before that date. Mill rates change by year, so check the city's current page for the rate on your bill.

  • Tax Collector phone: 203-630-4053, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Ask the title company to order a lien search for taxes and water and sewer charges.
  • Request payoff figures from the tax office before closing day.

The seller pays Connecticut's conveyance tax when the deed is recorded with the town clerk. Under C.G.S. 12-494, the standard split is 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the municipality, with a higher state rate on the part of a residential price above $800,000. A targeted investment community may add up to another one-quarter of one percent.

No clerk may record the deed until the return is filed and the tax is paid. Principal residences sold in lieu of foreclosure, and certain homes with defective pyrrhotite foundations, have their own exemption rules.

Many Meriden homes were built when the factories were running, so older systems, mixed-use buildings and multi-family houses are common. Owners inheriting a house, landlords tired of repairs, and homeowners behind on taxes or water bills are frequent sellers.

If taxes or water charges are unpaid, a lien can attach and the city can pursue it, so deal with it early. An as-is cash sale can pay those items off from the proceeds at closing, as long as the numbers work. Expect a cash buyer to tour the house, make a written offer and order a title search, after which the closing attorney prepares the deed and the conveyance tax return.

  • Pull your tax and water and sewer balance from the city.
  • Check for open permits with the building department.
  • Sort out title and heirs before you sign anything.

faqs.q: Is Meriden between New Haven and Hartford?
faqs.a: Yes. Meriden is in New Haven County about halfway between the two cities, and Interstate 91 and the Hartford Line rail service both connect it to them.

faqs.q: How often are Meriden real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: In four equal installments, in July, October, January and April. The city mails bills once a year, in July.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Meriden taxes?
faqs.a: Late taxes accrue interest at 1.5 percent a month, and unpaid real estate taxes must be liened by the end of the year they are due. The city may also refuse building permits for the property.

faqs.q: Did Meriden revalue its property recently?
faqs.a: Yes. The latest revaluation applies to the October 1, 2025 Grand List.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance tax when a Meriden house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays at recording, normally 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town on a standard home sale. Ask your attorney whether any extra municipal tax or exemption applies.
